requirement_text.REQ-047: Port src/engine/instance.zig's InstanceStore.applyTransition() as the persistence orchestration layer that turns REQ-044's pure transition output into committed rows -- task activation. Full design in lib/letflow/design/req047-task-activation-persistence.md, validated PASS by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (see step-01b handoff).

task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/req047-task-activation-persistence.md exactly as designed. Verify branch first (git branch --show-current must equal feature/WF02-REQ047-20260818). Implement Letflow.Engine.TaskActivation and wire it into Letflow.Engine.persist/7's Multi chain per the design. mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix ecto.migrate if any migration is needed (design should clarify whether the tasks table already has all needed columns from REQ-043 -- if so no new migration), mix format --check-formatted. Self-review per WF-02 Step 2a's checklist: no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user input, every state transition persisted via Letflow.Repo inside the transition, one supervised process per instance preserved if touching process_instance.ex/instance_supervisor.ex (this requirement should not touch those), new public functions have a one-line @doc, all callers of any changed function signature still compile.
acceptance_criteria: a transition that enters a HUMAN_TASK node results in exactly one tasks row with status PENDING carrying instance_id, node_id, node_name, assignee_type and assignee_ref, committed in the same transaction as the instance_projections update and the appended event
when the event append fails, zero tasks rows and zero instance_projections changes are committed -- demonstrated by forcing an append failure and reading all three tables back

transitions entering START, END, EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY and PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes create zero tasks rows, each with its own explicit test, verifying (not merely assuming) the transition function's pending_task_nodes guarantee
a HUMAN_TASK whose assignee_ref names a group with no members still produces a PENDING task rather than an activation error
a token entering an END node sets the instance to COMPLETED, creates no task, and leaves a documented named hook for SCH-03 timer cancellation with S6 identified as its owning stage
all existing callers of any changed function signature still compile

result.summary: Implemented REQ-047 per lib/letflow/design/req047-task-activation-persistence.md exactly. New module lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex (Letflow.Engine.TaskActivation): token_id_to_record_id/2 (zips new_instance_state.tokens with M2's inserted TokenRecord list), newly_pending_tokens/2 (set-diff by token_id, resolving REQ-044's open pending_task_nodes-tracking question per design §5.1), resolve_assignee/1 (reads node.attributes['role']/['assignee_type'], zero group-membership resolution, satisfying AC4), insert_attrs/4 (six-key attrs map, node_name falls back to node.id when node.label is nil per design §4.2/OQ-2), append_multi/6 (appends one Multi.run(:task_records, ...) step to the caller's Ecto.Multi, short-circuits on first failure via Enum.reduce_while, returns {:error,{:missing_token_record,_}} / {:error,{:unknown_node_id,_}} rather than raising), and cancel_pending_timers/2 (the named SCH-03/S6 hook, unconditional :ok body, moduledoc/doc text naming S6 as owner verbatim per design §8). Zero Repo calls inside TaskActivation itself (INV-EE47-7) -- all writes happen inside the caller's already-open Multi/transaction. Wired into lib/letflow/engine.ex: persist/7 became persist/8 (added a `graph` parameter, threaded from a new activate/3 return value {:ok, graph, new_instance_state} instead of {:ok, new_instance_state} -- both are private functions with no external callers, confirmed by grep). The Multi chain gained TaskActivation.append_multi(instance_id, graph, [], new_instance_state, prefix) positioned after :token_record (M2) and before :event (M3), matching design §1's documented ordering; create/2's own call site always passes [] as previous_pending_task_nodes since a freshly-constructed InstanceState always starts with pending_task_nodes: [] (design §5.1). finalize_instance_projection/4 became /5 (added instance_id) and now calls `:ok = TaskActivation.cancel_pending_timers(instance_id, prefix)` inside the :completed clause, immediately after the status flip to :completed, still inside the open transaction (design §8). No migration added -- confirmed against priv/repo/migrations/ (20260818110003_create_tasks.exs already has every column this design writes: instance_id, token_id, node_id, node_name, assignee_type, assignee_ref, status default :pending) and design §9's own explicit statement that no migration is needed. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` output: 'Compiling 1 file (.ex)\nGenerated letflow app' -- exit 0, zero warnings. `mix format --check-formatted` on the two touched files (lib/letflow/engine.ex, lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex) after running `mix format` on them: 'FORMATTED_OK' -- exit 0 (the two files needed reformatting after edits, matching this project's existing convention; several other pre-existing files in the repo are also currently unformatted -- transition.ex, identity_migration.ex, and several test files -- left untouched as out of this requirement's scope). Ran the existing engine test suite to confirm no call-site breakage: `mix test test/letflow/engine/` -> '1 property, 125 tests, 0 failures'. `mix test test/letflow/engine_test.exs` fails to compile with a pre-existing SystemLimitError (a test name over 255 chars) -- confirmed via `git stash`/re-run that this failure exists identically on the pre-change tree, unrelated to this run's changes, not reworked here. No new test files were written (TEST-DESIGNER's job per Step 2a's own instruction).
issues: Pre-existing SystemLimitError in test/letflow/engine_test.exs (test name >255 chars) blocks that file's compilation -- confirmed present before this run's changes via git stash; not this requirement's own scope to fix, flagging for TEST-RUNNER/TEST-DESIGNER awareness.
